text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonia won second place in the European decathlon championship yesterday
- Female members of Nordic centre parties met in Estonia's Laulasmaa resort over the weekend.
- Lithuania won the Baltic firemen's championship.
- The town of Sillamae is celebrating its 40th jubilee. It was founded in 1947.
- The August 22 Michael Jackson concert will employ more than 1,000 Estonian residents, half of them for security.
- Riigikogu extra session today will concentrate on laws necessary for European integration.
- The National Defence Academy began a three-week chaplains' training course. There are 15 candidates.
- The first wave of admission to the EU will not take place before 2005, Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves said in Amsterdam.
- A popular protest meeting took place in Otepae on Saturday against the selling of a beach area to rich private owners, who would close it to public access.
- The shareholders of the confectionery factory Kalev decided on Friday to pay 22 kroons dividends per share.
- Finnish concern Partek bought a 33 percent of Rakke lime plant's shares.
